question: According to Ethan Evans, what should a leader do to recover after a major failure and rebuild trust?
expected_points: Own the mistake and avoid deflecting.
Set priorities and keep people updated regularly.
Work quickly and pull in the help needed to fix the problem.
evidence_quote: When you have a mistake, it's on you to pull out the stops, even if it's uncomfortable to recover from it.

answer.summary: Own the failure, move quickly to fix it, keep people updated so they can see the team is on it, and face the people affected. Trust may need to be earned back through reliable action and follow-through.

sections.heading: Take ownership and fix the problem
sections.content: Ethan says to work hard and fast: pull out the stops to recover, even when it is uncomfortable, rather than waiting until Monday. In his case, the team worked through a difficult weekend, brought in help, and sent people home to sleep in shifts. He describes doing the hard recovery work as part of showing ownership.

sections.heading: Communicate progress and rebuild trust incrementally
sections.content: Keep people informed about what is happening and what the priorities are. In the failure he describes, hourly updates helped others see that the team was on the problem; Ethan says this let them wait another hour without stepping in, so he was rebuilding trust “one hour at a time” and avoiding multiple layers of management piling on.

sections.heading: Face the people affected and show what comes next
sections.content: Rather than avoiding an angry leader, meet them directly. When Jeff Bezos asked how he was doing, Ethan acknowledged that the week had been hard and explained what they were doing and what they would do in the future. He says he still had to re-earn trust: he showed he had learned to launch more reliably, and was promoted two years later.

sections.heading: Do not let shame end the recovery
sections.content: Ethan says he could admit he had made a mistake while still recognizing that he was a good person and worker, then move on. He notes that others in his position might have quit, but he did not let shame stop him.

The answer says to communicate priorities and keep people updated, including hourly updates, covering both setting priorities and regular communication.
